question: Who among the following has the power to grant pardons under Article 161 of the Constitution of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: President
Chief Justice of India
Governor
Prime Minister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Governor

Explanation:
Under Article 161 of the Constitution of India, the Governor of a state has the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment for offenses against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the state extends. This power is similar to the President's power under Article 72, but it applies only to state-level offenses. The Governor exercises this power on the advice of the Council of Ministers of the state. However, this power is subject to judicial review and cannot be exercised arbitrarily. The Governor can grant pardons in cases involving state laws, but not in cases involving central laws or military courts. The distinction between the pardoning powers of the President and the Governor is important for federal governance.

☛ Under which article does the Governor have the pardoning power? → Article 161
☛ What are the types of pardoning powers? → Pardon, reprieve, respite, remission, and commutation
☛ Is the Governor's pardoning power absolute? → No, it is subject to judicial review
☛ Whose advice does the Governor need to grant a pardon? → Council of Ministers

question: Who among the following is considered as the first Law Officer of Government of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/04/2021) Shift 2)
options: Solicitor-General
Senior most Advocate of Supreme Court
Attorney - General
Chief Justice of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Attorney - General

Explanation:
According to Article 76 of the Indian Constitution, the Attorney-General is the highest law officer of the Government of India. He is appointed by the President and advises the government on legal matters. The Attorney-General has the right to participate in the proceedings of Parliament but cannot vote. He represents the government in the Supreme Court. The Solicitor-General works under the Attorney-General. The senior-most advocate of the Supreme Court is a title, while the Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary, not a law officer of the government. Thus, the first Law Officer of the Government of India is the Attorney-General.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किसे भारत सरकार का प्रथम विधि अधिकारी माना जाता है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/04/2021) Shift 2)

Explanation:
भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 76 के अनुसार, अटॉर्नी-जनरल भारत सरकार का सर्वोच्च विधि अधिकारी होता है। उन्हें भारत के राष्ट्रपति द्वारा नियुक्त किया जाता है और वे सरकार को कानूनी मामलों में सलाह देते हैं। अटॉर्नी-जनरल को संसद की कार्यवाही में भाग लेने का अधिकार है, लेकिन वे मतदान नहीं कर सकते। वे सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में सरकार की ओर से पैरवी करते हैं। सॉलिसिटर-जनरल अटॉर्नी-जनरल के अधीन कार्य करता है। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के वरिष्ठ अधिवक्ता एक पद है, जबकि मुख्य न्यायाधीश न्यायपालिका का प्रमुख होता है, सरकार का विधि अधिकारी नहीं। इस प्रकार, भारत सरकार का प्रथम विधि अधिकारी अटॉर्नी-जनरल है।

question: Which part of the Constitution of India has been influenced by the German Constitution? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Single citizenship
Federal system
Amendment of the Constitution
Suspension of fundamental rights during Emergency
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Suspension of fundamental rights during Emergency

Explanation:
The emergency provisions of the Indian Constitution are influenced by the German Constitution (Weimar Constitution). The German Constitution had provisions for suspending fundamental rights during an emergency, which was adopted in the Indian Constitution under Article 359. In India, the President can suspend fundamental rights during an emergency, except for Articles 20 and 21. Other options: Single citizenship is influenced by Britain, federal system by Canada, and amendment procedure by South Africa.

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का आपातकालीन प्रावधान जर्मन संविधान (वाइमर संविधान) से प्रभावित है। जर्मन संविधान में आपातकाल के दौरान मौलिक अधिकारों को निलंबित करने का प्रावधान था, जिसे भारतीय संविधान में अनुच्छेद 359 के तहत लिया गया। भारत में राष्ट्रपति आपातकाल के दौरान मौलिक अधिकारों को निलंबित कर सकते हैं, हालांकि अनुच्छेद 20 और 21 को निलंबित नहीं किया जा सकता। अन्य विकल्प: एकल नागरिकता ब्रिटेन से, संघीय प्रणाली कनाडा से, और संविधान में संशोधन दक्षिण अफ्रीका से प्रभावित है।

question: If the period of Lok Sabha is extended due to the National Emergency and when the Emergency is over, how long will the extended period be? (RPF SI 2018 (13/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: 3 Months
6 Months
2 Months
1 year
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 6 Months

Explanation:
Under Article 83(2) of the Indian Constitution, the normal term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years. However, during a National Emergency, Parliament may extend the term by law for up to 1 year at a time. The extended term can continue only for up to 6 months after the Emergency ceases to operate. This provision ensures that elections are held promptly after the Emergency ends. Thus, the correct answer is 6 months.

☛ Maximum extension per occasion during National Emergency → 1 year
☛ Maximum extended period after Emergency ends → 6 months
☛ Related Article → Article 83(2)
☛ Applies to → Lok Sabha only
question_hi: यदि राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल के कारण लोक सभा की अवधि बढ़ा दी जाती है और जब आपातकाल समाप्त हो जाता है, तो बढ़ाई गई अवधि कितनी होगी? (RPF SI 2018 (13/01/2019) Shift 2)

6 माह
2 माह
1 वर्ष

Solution: सही उत्तर है 6 माह

Explanation:

question: Which House is headed by Speaker from both Houses of Indian Parliament?  (RPF SI 2018 (11/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Lok Sabha
Viceroy House
Gram Sabha
Rajya Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lok Sabha

Explanation:
The Indian Parliament consists of two houses - Lok Sabha (Lower House) and Rajya Sabha (Upper House). The presiding officer of Lok Sabha is the Speaker, who conducts the proceedings and maintains the dignity of the House. Rajya Sabha is presided over by the Vice President, who is the ex-officio Chairman of that House. Thus, the Speaker heads only Lok Sabha, not Rajya Sabha. question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution permits the Supreme Court to review its judgement or order?  (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (17/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Article 137
Article 138
Article 132
Article 135
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 137

Explanation:
Article 137 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to review any of its judgments or orders. This is a special power that allows the Court to reconsider a case if it believes that it is necessary in the interest of justice. This provision is a crucial part of judicial review and ensures that the Court can correct any mistakes. Article 137 grants the Supreme Court the authority to review its decisions, but this power is not available to lower courts. Petitions filed under this Article are called 'review petitions'. According to the Supreme Court Rules, a review petition is accepted only in exceptional circumstances, such as when there is an error apparent on the face of the record or a miscarriage of justice. The review power is not an appeal but a reconsideration of the same case.

question: What happens if a minister is not a member of the Parliament for six consecutive months? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 2)

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides guidelines for states to make laws on the protection of monuments and objects of national importance? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (23/06/2025) Shift 2)

question: The _______ has the authority to punish for contempt of court in India. (RRB Paramedical (11/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: President of India
Parliament of India
Supreme Court and High Courts
Lok Adalat
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Supreme Court and High Courts

Explanation:
Under Articles 129 and 215 of the Indian Constitution, the Supreme Court and High Courts have the authority to punish for contempt of court. Contempt is of two types: civil contempt (willful disobedience of a court order) and criminal contempt (acts that scandalize or lower the authority of the court). This power is essential to maintain the independence and dignity of the judiciary. Though Parliament enacted the Contempt of Courts Act in 1971, the power to punish remains with the courts. The President or Lok Adalat does not possess this power.

☛ What is civil contempt? → Willful disobedience of court orders
☛ What is criminal contempt? → Acts harming court's prestige
☛ Can Parliament punish for contempt of court? → No, only courts have this power
☛ When was the Contempt of Courts Act enacted? → 1971
question_hi: भारत में न्यायालय की अवमानना ​​के लिए दंडित करने का अधिकार _______ के पास है। (RRB Paramedical (11/03/2026) Shift 3)

question: What is the main role of the Finance Commission in Centre-State relations in India? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Allocating state shares of GST
Recommending distribution between the Union and the States of the net proceeds of taxes
Approving state budgets
Planning economic development funds
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Recommending distribution between the Union and the States of the net proceeds of taxes

Explanation:
Established under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution, the Finance Commission is a constitutional body whose primary role is to recommend the distribution of net tax proceeds between the Union and the States. The Commission is constituted every five years and provides recommendations on the sharing of financial resources, grants-in-aid, and the financial needs of states. Its objective is to maintain balance in Centre-State financial relations and ensure adequate resources for states. Allocation of state shares in GST is done by the GST Council, while state budgets are approved by the respective state legislatures. Planning of economic development funds is related to the Planning Commission or NITI Aayog.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ What is the tenure of the Finance Commission? → Five years
☛ Which Finance Commission is currently (2024) in place? → 16th Finance Commission
☛ Who are the recommendations of the Finance Commission binding on? → Central Government
☛ Who decides financial matters related to GST? → GST Council

Explanation:

question: Which Constitutional provision empowers the Government of India to give directions to a State in certain matters? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Article 256
Article 248
Article 262
Article 265
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 256

Explanation:
Article 256 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Government of India to give directions to a State for ensuring compliance with laws made by Parliament. This provision strengthens Centre-State relations within the federal framework. If a State fails to implement central laws, the Centre can issue necessary directions. It is related to Article 257, which allows the Centre to direct States in national interest. Article 248 pertains to residuary legislative powers of Parliament, Article 262 deals with inter-state water disputes, and Article 265 requires a law for taxation. Thus, only Article 256 fits the context.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article 256 → Empowers Centre to give directions to States for legal compliance.
☛ Article 248 → Confers residuary legislative powers on Parliament.
☛ Article 262 → Relates to adjudication of inter-state water disputes.
☛ Article 265 → States that no tax shall be levied without authority of law.
☛ Article 257 → Provides for Centre's directions to States in national interest.

question: All other ministers, including the Prime Minister, are collectively responsible for __________.  (RPF SI 2018 (13/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Lok Sabha
Political Party
President
Rajya Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lok Sabha

Explanation:
According to Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. This means that all ministers, including the Prime Minister, are jointly accountable to the Lok Sabha. This is a fundamental principle of the parliamentary system of government where the executive is responsible to the legislature. If a no-confidence motion is passed against the Council of Ministers in the Lok Sabha, the entire council must resign. This system ensures the accountability of the government to the people's representatives.

question: Which of the following parts/provisions of the Constitution of India CANNOT be amended? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/04/2021) Shift 2)
options: Judicial review
Preamble to the Constitution
Directive Principles of State Policy
Fundamental rights
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Judicial review

Explanation:
In the Kesavananda Bharati case, the Supreme Court established the basic structure doctrine, declaring that certain features of the Constitution cannot be amended. Judicial review, which allows courts to examine laws' constitutionality under Articles 13 and 32, is a part of this basic structure. The Preamble has been amended (42nd Amendment added socialist, secular). Fundamental Rights (Articles 14-35) and Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36-51) can be amended as long as they do not violate the basic structure. Thus, judicial review cannot be abolished even by Parliament.

☛ What limits amendments to Fundamental Rights? → Must not violate basic structure
☛ What is the source of Directive Principles? → Irish Constitution

question: The provision of 'Impeachment of President' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of _____. (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (02/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: United States of America
Canada
Britain
French
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is United States of America

Explanation:
The provision of impeachment of the President in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the United States of America. It is detailed in Article 61, which lays down the procedure for removing the President for violation of the Constitution. The impeachment process can be initiated in either House of Parliament and requires a special majority. In the US Constitution, this process applies to the President, Vice President, and other federal officers, whereas in India it applies only to the President. This provision is not subject to judicial review, similar to the US system. The Indian Constitution has borrowed many features from various countries, and this procedure from the US is a significant one.

question: In what way does the Union Cabinet differ from other government committees? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: It functions independently of the Prime Minister
It serves as the supreme decision-making body of the executive branch
It is elected by the public
It includes members of the judiciary
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It serves as the supreme decision-making body of the executive branch

Explanation:
The Union Cabinet is the highest decision-making body in the executive branch of the Indian government, operating under Articles 74 and 75 of the Constitution. Unlike other government committees, the Cabinet is chaired by the Prime Minister and determines major policies. It is collectively responsible to the Parliament, and its members are appointed by the Prime Minister, not elected by the public. The Cabinet does not include judiciary members. Its meetings are confidential, and its decisions are binding on all ministers. This distinguishes it from other committees, which are often advisory or subordinate. The Cabinet exercises real executive power and coordinates government functions.

solution_hi:

केंद्रीय मंत्रिमंडल भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 74 और 75 के तहत कार्यपालिका का सर्वोच्च निकाय है। यह प्रधानमंत्री की अध्यक्षता में कार्य करता है और महत्वपूर्ण नीतिगत निर्णय लेता है। अन्य सरकारी समितियों के विपरीत, मंत्रिमंडल सामूहिक रूप से संसद के प्रति उत्तरदायी होता है। इसके सदस्य प्रधानमंत्री द्वारा नियुक्त किए जाते हैं, जनता द्वारा नहीं, और इसमें न्यायपालिका के सदस्य शामिल नहीं होते। मंत्रिमंडल की बैठकें गुप्त होती हैं और इसके निर्णय सभी मंत्रियों पर बाध्यकारी होते हैं। यह संघीय कार्यपालिका का वास्तविक शक्ति का केंद्र है।
